1	# Cerne — Requirements and Screen Flow
2	
3	Cerne is a reflective-journaling mobile app with an AI assistant. The user records their day by text, audio or photo; a conversational agent consults those records (semantic search) to answer with context and to offer insights.
4	
5	This document is the product specification. The visual reference is the prototype in `docs/input/prototype/`; the backend API is documented in `docs/input/backend/`.
6	
7	---
8	
9	## 1. Functional requirements
10	
11	### RF01 — Multimodal capture (text / audio / photo)
12	Data entry by text, real-time audio recording and photo upload — always through Screen 2 (Insertion Modal), which has a raw text field in addition to the microphone and the gallery. Every capture becomes a persisted record (`POST /entries`), **distinct from a chat message** (see the separation note in RF04).
13	
14	**Acceptance criteria:**
15	- The three modalities (text, audio, photo) result in the same persisted-entry format — none is treated structurally differently from the others after capture.
16	- Cancelling a capture midway (e.g., interrupting a recording) does not create a partial or empty entry.
17	
18	### RF02 — Speech-to-text / OCR processing
19	Transcription of audio (speech-to-text) and recognition of text in images (OCR) over the content captured in RF01.
20	
21	**Acceptance criteria:** four visible states — recording, processing, transcribed, transcription error.
22	
23	### RF03 — Biometric authentication vault
24	Access barrier via Face ID / Touch ID / PIN before exposing the user's data.
25	
26	**Acceptance criteria:**
27	- A biometric failure (e.g., fingerprint not recognized) offers PIN as an alternative, without locking the user out of the app.
28	- The app, sent to the background and resumed after 5 minutes, requires authentication again — it does not stay unlocked indefinitely (fixed value, not configurable by the user).
29	
30	### RF04 — Interactive chat with memory (RAG)
31	Continuous conversation with the AI agent, with semantic search over previous entries. **Chat messages are conversational and do not create journal entries automatically** — the only exception is the explicit save action described in RF10. Otherwise, the chat queries existing entries via RAG but does not write to them.
32	
33	**Acceptance criteria:**
34	- Three mandatory UI states: processing/streaming, error, complete response.
35	- If the response stream drops midway, the partial message stays visible with a failure indication (it does not disappear).
36	
37	### RF05 — Personal summary export
38	Generation of a narrative summary by AI (Claude Haiku 4.5) from the user's entries, exportable as PDF, with an additional option to download the raw data without the narrative. No clinical or diagnostic connotation. **Scope: job generation, file download and failure handling — never the quality of the generated narrative text.**
39	
40	**Acceptance criteria:**
41	- An export job with zero entries in the period returns a handled error state (not an empty PDF, not a crash).
42	- A failure generating the narrative text (model timeout) still allows downloading the raw data without the narrative — the export is not blocked by an AI failure.
43	
44	### RF06 — Semantic search / filter over journal entries
45	Semantic similarity search (via Voyage AI embeddings, reusing the ones already generated in RF01) combined with metadata filters (date, entry type). There is no filter by tag or category: the backend does not implement it in any endpoint — `GET /entries` and `GET /entries/search` accept only `source` and `dateFrom`/`dateTo`. Tags appear only embedded, read-only, in the `Entry` object (see section 2).
46	
47	**Acceptance criteria:**
48	- Searching for a term finds semantically related entries even without the exact word (e.g., searching "ansiedade" returns an entry that only mentions "nervosismo", without the literal term).
49	- 300 ms search debounce: fast typing triggers a single query, not one per keystroke.
50	- Results from the local read cache stay consistent with the server after reconnection, without duplicating displayed items *(the architecture is cloud-only; offline allows only viewing already-cached data, not writing)*.
51	- Two or more filters applied at the same time (`source` + `dateFrom`/`dateTo`) narrow results with AND logic (not OR).
52	- Clearing the filters returns to the full list without restarting the screen.
53	
54	### RF07 — Multi-source history (timeline)
55	A screen whose state depends simultaneously on authentication, synchronization status and entry data.
56	
57	**Acceptance criteria:**
58	- Session expiration while viewing triggers a new-login prompt without a crash and without losing the scroll position.
59	- The per-entry synchronization status badge updates independently of the authentication stream.
60	- No BLoC imports another BLoC directly.
61	
62	### RF08 — Proactive insights (mechanism)
63	A suggestion inserted into the chat without the user asking for it. **Scope: only the trigger mechanism, never the quality of the generated text.**
64	
65	**Acceptance criteria:**
66	- Trigger after N = 5 user messages OR T = 2 min of inactivity — fires exactly once per satisfied condition.
67	- If insight generation fails (timeout / network error), the main chat keeps working normally.
68	- Dismissing the insight does not change the scroll position or the state of the main conversation.
69	
70	### RF09 — Temporal summaries / dashboard
71	An evolution chart with a textual summary, computed on demand when the Settings tab is opened. **Scope: aggregation and rendering, never the quality of the narrative text.**
72	
73	**Acceptance criteria:**
74	- Renders correctly in three scenarios: zero entries, one entry, more than 30 entries.
75	- The aggregation recalculates correctly after an entry is created (cache-invalidation test). Entries are immutable: there is no `PATCH /entries/:id` or `DELETE /entries/:id` in the backend, and no screen describes an edit or delete action on an entry.
76	- The AI narrative text is checked only for not breaking the UI in extreme cases — never for its content.
77	
78	### RF10 — Save a chat message as an entry
79	A button on each user message in the chat that converts it into a persisted entry — for moments when the user states relevant information during the conversation, not only through dedicated capture (RF01). It reuses the same `POST /entries` pipeline (PII check + embedding), with the origin marked as `chat`.
80	
81	**Acceptance criteria:**
82	- The chat feature triggers the creation of the entry through a shared interface / use case, never by directly importing a repository or data source of the entries feature — a violation here also breaks RNF06.
83	- Saving the same message twice does not create duplicate entries (idempotency).
84	- A failure to save (network unavailable) keeps the conversation working normally, and the button returns to a state that allows trying again — the same failure-isolation pattern as RF08.
85	- Only user messages have the button — AI responses cannot become entries.
86	
87	---
88	
89	## 2. Extension features — not implemented
90	
91	They keep the "essence" of the original product flow and exist in the prototype, but **receive no functional implementation**. A menu entry may exist as a placeholder.
92	
93	| Original feature | Treatment in the current version |
94	|---|---|
95	| Dynamic categorization (AI) | Simplified to manual tags created by the user (My Records screen) |
96	| Autonomous goal extraction | Action Plans screen — static, no logic |
97	| Dynamic persona adjustment | Simple cosmetic toggle (Settings), low cost to maintain |
98	
99	---
100	
101	## 3. Quality requirements
102	
103	| ID | Requirement | Target |
104	|---|---|---|
105	| RNF06 | Zero layer violations — the domain layer does not import `package:flutter` nor classes from `data/` | 0 violations |
106	| RNF07 | Minimum test coverage of the domain layer (`lib/**/domain/**`) | ≥ 80% |
107	| RNF08 | Visual fidelity to the prototype — the primary color matches the prototype's hex value, typography matches family and size, spacing matches the prototype; no visual value hardcoded outside the central file `design_tokens.dart` | Every screen faithful in color, typography and spacing; 0 hardcoded values |
108	| RNF09 | Consistent network-error handling — `Either<Failure, T>` pattern via `fpdart` in every repository; every write endpoint (5 endpoints) handles three failure types — timeout, malformed response, no connection — covered by tests with `mocktail` | 0 repository signatures outside the pattern; 15 of 15 scenarios handled |
109	
110	## 4. Other non-functional requirements
111	
112	RNF01 — Interaction latency (a local action is reflected in the UI in < 100 ms; any network call above 300 ms shows a loading indicator) · RNF02 — PII stripping (via Claude Haiku 4.5 with a structured prompt / tool use, not a dedicated NER model) · RNF03 — Zero data retention · RNF04 — RLS (Row Level Security) · RNF05 — Hard delete of account and data (LGPD).
113	
114	**Known limitation:** the system has no protocol for detecting or responding to risk signals (suicidal ideation, self-harm) in entries or chat messages. Since the product is not framed as a mental-health app, this absence is an explicit scope decision.
115	
116	---
117	
118	## 5. Interface architecture and screen flow
119	
120	### 5.1 Visual foundation (design system)
121	Minimalist identity, a warm and neutral palette, readable sans-serif typography, standardized components (buttons, chat bubbles, cards). This foundation is the direct object of RNF08. Tokens: `docs/input/prototype/prototype-extract.md`.
122	
123	### 5.2 Screens
124	
125	**Screen 0 — Splash:** initial loading; checks the connection and syncs the cache in the background. *Connects to: RF06, RNF01.*
126	
127	**Screen 0.1 — Authentication vault:** biometric/PIN barrier before access. *Connects to: RF03.*
128	
129	**Screen 1 — Home (chat):** main screen, continuous conversation, "+" button for multimodal input, AI status indicator, "save to journal" button on each user message. *Connects to: RF04, RF08, RF10, RNF01, RNF09.*
130	
131	**Screen 2 — Insertion Modal:** overlay with three ways to capture — raw text field, microphone (audio) and gallery/camera (photo) — with a transcription indicator. Every capture here creates a persisted entry, never a chat message. *Connects to: RF01, RF02.*
132	
133	**Screen 3 — Side menu (sidebar):** navigation hub, session history, access to My Records / Action Plans / Settings, and a "Novo Chat" button that opens Screen 1 in its empty state. *Connects to: RF04 (via the "Novo Chat" button); the other items are pure navigation.*
134	
135	**Screen 4 — My Records:** consolidated timeline, filters, manual tags (extension, section 2), export. *Connects to: RF07, RF06, RF05.*
136	
137	**Screen 5 — Action Plans:** simple Kanban board (columns "A Fazer" / "Em Andamento" / "Concluído") with static example cards. *(Extension — section 2.)*
138	
139	**Screen 6 — Settings and profile:** evolution dashboard, persona selector — "Analítico" / "Empático" / "Socrático" (extension, section 2; it would only change the system-prompt string of RF04), delete account. *Connects to: RF09, RNF05.*
140	
141	---
142	
143	## 6. Backend endpoint inventory
144	
145	The backend is already built and frozen. The API contract, `docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml`, is the source of truth; this section is a reading of it oriented by screen and requirement. How to build the real URL of each operation: `docs/input/backend/README.md`.
146	
147	Every endpoint returns errors in the standard contract of RNF09 — `{ code, message, retryable }` — and is protected by RLS in Supabase. AI providers: Claude (chat, vision/OCR, summary, insights, dashboard, PII detection) and Voyage AI (embeddings) — the backend's only two external AI dependencies. Audio transcription (speech-to-text) runs on-device (Whisper) and never reaches the backend as an audio file.
148	
149	### 6.1 Authentication and session
150	| Endpoint | Requirement | AI involved |
151	|---|---|---|
152	| `POST /auth/signup` | RF03 | — |
153	| `POST /auth/login` | RF03 | — |
154	| `POST /auth/refresh` | RF03, RF07 | — |
155	| `GET /auth/session` | RF07 | — |
156	| `POST /auth/logout` | RF03 | — |
157	
158	**No "biometric-unlock" endpoint — intentional:** the Face ID / Touch ID / PIN barrier of Screen 0.1 is validated entirely on the device, never on the server. The backend only stores the preference (`biometricEnabled`, read and written via `PATCH /account/settings`, section 6.7) — it validates no biometrics. After passing the local barrier, the app uses the existing session (renewed via `POST /auth/refresh` when needed, or `POST /auth/login` if it has fully expired).
159	
160	### 6.2 Ingestion and entries
161	| Endpoint | Requirement | AI involved |
162	|---|---|---|
163	| `POST /media/ocr` — the image is not persisted; only the extracted text moves on | RF02 | Claude Haiku 4.5 (vision) |
164	| `POST /entries` — creates an entry; internally triggers the PII check and embedding generation; accepts `source` (`manual`/`audio`/`photo`/`chat`) and `chatMessageId` when the origin is the chat | RF01, RF02, RF10 | Claude Haiku 4.5 (PII) + Voyage AI (embedding) |
165	| `GET /entries` — filters by `source`/`dateFrom`/`dateTo`; tags appear only embedded in the response, read-only | RF07 | — |
166	| `GET /entries/:id` | RF07 | — |
167	
168	**No entry editing or deletion, and no tag endpoint — intentional:** entries are immutable once created ("original content intact, never censored"); there is no `PATCH`/`DELETE /entries/:id`. Tags are populated only by test seed data — no endpoint creates, deletes or filters by tag or category (see RF06). This is consistent with section 2: dynamic categorization was simplified to manual tags that receive no functional implementation.
169	
170	### 6.3 Chat and memory (RAG)
171	| Endpoint | Requirement | AI involved |
172	|---|---|---|
173	| `POST /chat/sessions` — blocked offline | RF04 | — |
174	| `GET /chat/sessions` — works offline (cache) | RF04, RF07 | — |
175	| `GET /chat/sessions/:id/messages` — works offline (cache) | RF04 | — |

# Cerne — Requirements and Screen Flow

Cerne is a reflective-journaling mobile app with an AI assistant. The user records their day by text, audio or photo; a conversational agent consults those records (semantic search) to answer with context and to offer insights.

This document is the product specification. The visual reference is the prototype in `docs/input/prototype/`; the backend API is documented in `docs/input/backend/`.

---

## 1. Functional requirements

### RF01 — Multimodal capture (text / audio / photo)
Data entry by text, real-time audio recording and photo upload — always through Screen 2 (Insertion Modal), which has a raw text field in addition to the microphone and the gallery. Every capture becomes a persisted record (`POST /entries`), **distinct from a chat message** (see the separation note in RF04).

**Acceptance criteria:**
- The three modalities (text, audio, photo) result in the same persisted-entry format — none is treated structurally differently from the others after capture.
- Cancelling a capture midway (e.g., interrupting a recording) does not create a partial or empty entry.

### RF02 — Speech-to-text / OCR processing
Transcription of audio (speech-to-text) and recognition of text in images (OCR) over the content captured in RF01.

**Acceptance criteria:** four visible states — recording, processing, transcribed, transcription error.

### RF03 — Biometric authentication vault
Access barrier via Face ID / Touch ID / PIN before exposing the user's data.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- A biometric failure (e.g., fingerprint not recognized) offers PIN as an alternative, without locking the user out of the app.
- The app, sent to the background and resumed after 5 minutes, requires authentication again — it does not stay unlocked indefinitely (fixed value, not configurable by the user).

### RF04 — Interactive chat with memory (RAG)
Continuous conversation with the AI agent, with semantic search over previous entries. **Chat messages are conversational and do not create journal entries automatically** — the only exception is the explicit save action described in RF10. Otherwise, the chat queries existing entries via RAG but does not write to them.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Three mandatory UI states: processing/streaming, error, complete response.
- If the response stream drops midway, the partial message stays visible with a failure indication (it does not disappear).

### RF05 — Personal summary export
Generation of a narrative summary by AI (Claude Haiku 4.5) from the user's entries, exportable as PDF, with an additional option to download the raw data without the narrative. No clinical or diagnostic connotation. **Scope: job generation, file download and failure handling — never the quality of the generated narrative text.**

**Acceptance criteria:**
- An export job with zero entries in the period returns a handled error state (not an empty PDF, not a crash).
- A failure generating the narrative text (model timeout) still allows downloading the raw data without the narrative — the export is not blocked by an AI failure.

### RF06 — Semantic search / filter over journal entries
Semantic similarity search (via Voyage AI embeddings, reusing the ones already generated in RF01) combined with metadata filters (date, entry type). There is no filter by tag or category: the backend does not implement it in any endpoint — `GET /entries` and `GET /entries/search` accept only `source` and `dateFrom`/`dateTo`. Tags appear only embedded, read-only, in the `Entry` object (see section 2).

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Searching for a term finds semantically related entries even without the exact word (e.g., searching "ansiedade" returns an entry that only mentions "nervosismo", without the literal term).
- 300 ms search debounce: fast typing triggers a single query, not one per keystroke.
- Results from the local read cache stay consistent with the server after reconnection, without duplicating displayed items *(the architecture is cloud-only; offline allows only viewing already-cached data, not writing)*.
- Two or more filters applied at the same time (`source` + `dateFrom`/`dateTo`) narrow results with AND logic (not OR).
- Clearing the filters returns to the full list without restarting the screen.

### RF07 — Multi-source history (timeline)
A screen whose state depends simultaneously on authentication, synchronization status and entry data.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Session expiration while viewing triggers a new-login prompt without a crash and without losing the scroll position.
- The per-entry synchronization status badge updates independently of the authentication stream.
- No BLoC imports another BLoC directly.

### RF08 — Proactive insights (mechanism)
A suggestion inserted into the chat without the user asking for it. **Scope: only the trigger mechanism, never the quality of the generated text.**

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Trigger after N = 5 user messages OR T = 2 min of inactivity — fires exactly once per satisfied condition.
- If insight generation fails (timeout / network error), the main chat keeps working normally.
- Dismissing the insight does not change the scroll position or the state of the main conversation.

### RF09 — Temporal summaries / dashboard
An evolution chart with a textual summary, computed on demand when the Settings tab is opened. **Scope: aggregation and rendering, never the quality of the narrative text.**

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Renders correctly in three scenarios: zero entries, one entry, more than 30 entries.
- The aggregation recalculates correctly after an entry is created (cache-invalidation test). Entries are immutable: there is no `PATCH /entries/:id` or `DELETE /entries/:id` in the backend, and no screen describes an edit or delete action on an entry.
- The AI narrative text is checked only for not breaking the UI in extreme cases — never for its content.

### RF10 — Save a chat message as an entry
A button on each user message in the chat that converts it into a persisted entry — for moments when the user states relevant information during the conversation, not only through dedicated capture (RF01). It reuses the same `POST /entries` pipeline (PII check + embedding), with the origin marked as `chat`.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- The chat feature triggers the creation of the entry through a shared interface / use case, never by directly importing a repository or data source of the entries feature — a violation here also breaks RNF06.
- Saving the same message twice does not create duplicate entries (idempotency).
- A failure to save (network unavailable) keeps the conversation working normally, and the button returns to a state that allows trying again — the same failure-isolation pattern as RF08.
- Only user messages have the button — AI responses cannot become entries.

---

## 2. Extension features — not implemented

They keep the "essence" of the original product flow and exist in the prototype, but **receive no functional implementation**. A menu entry may exist as a placeholder.

| Original feature | Treatment in the current version |
|---|---|
| Dynamic categorization (AI) | Simplified to manual tags created by the user (My Records screen) |
| Autonomous goal extraction | Action Plans screen — static, no logic |
| Dynamic persona adjustment | Simple cosmetic toggle (Settings), low cost to maintain |

---

## 3. Quality requirements

| ID | Requirement | Target |
|---|---|---|
| RNF06 | Zero layer violations — the domain layer does not import `package:flutter` nor classes from `data/` | 0 violations |
| RNF07 | Minimum test coverage of the domain layer (`lib/**/domain/**`) | ≥ 80% |
| RNF08 | Visual fidelity to the prototype — the primary color matches the prototype's hex value, typography matches family and size, spacing matches the prototype; no visual value hardcoded outside the central file `design_tokens.dart` | Every screen faithful in color, typography and spacing; 0 hardcoded values |
| RNF09 | Consistent network-error handling — `Either<Failure, T>` pattern via `fpdart` in every repository; every write endpoint (5 endpoints) handles three failure types — timeout, malformed response, no connection — covered by tests with `mocktail` | 0 repository signatures outside the pattern; 15 of 15 scenarios handled |

## 4. Other non-functional requirements

RNF01 — Interaction latency (a local action is reflected in the UI in < 100 ms; any network call above 300 ms shows a loading indicator) · RNF02 — PII stripping (via Claude Haiku 4.5 with a structured prompt / tool use, not a dedicated NER model) · RNF03 — Zero data retention · RNF04 — RLS (Row Level Security) · RNF05 — Hard delete of account and data (LGPD).

**Known limitation:** the system has no protocol for detecting or responding to risk signals (suicidal ideation, self-harm) in entries or chat messages. Since the product is not framed as a mental-health app, this absence is an explicit scope decision.

---

## 5. Interface architecture and screen flow

### 5.1 Visual foundation (design system)
Minimalist identity, a warm and neutral palette, readable sans-serif typography, standardized components (buttons, chat bubbles, cards). This foundation is the direct object of RNF08. Tokens: `docs/input/prototype/prototype-extract.md`.

### 5.2 Screens

**Screen 0 — Splash:** initial loading; checks the connection and syncs the cache in the background. *Connects to: RF06, RNF01.*

**Screen 0.1 — Authentication vault:** biometric/PIN barrier before access. *Connects to: RF03.*

**Screen 1 — Home (chat):** main screen, continuous conversation, "+" button for multimodal input, AI status indicator, "save to journal" button on each user message. *Connects to: RF04, RF08, RF10, RNF01, RNF09.*

**Screen 2 — Insertion Modal:** overlay with three ways to capture — raw text field, microphone (audio) and gallery/camera (photo) — with a transcription indicator. Every capture here creates a persisted entry, never a chat message. *Connects to: RF01, RF02.*

**Screen 3 — Side menu (sidebar):** navigation hub, session history, access to My Records / Action Plans / Settings, and a "Novo Chat" button that opens Screen 1 in its empty state. *Connects to: RF04 (via the "Novo Chat" button); the other items are pure navigation.*

**Screen 4 — My Records:** consolidated timeline, filters, manual tags (extension, section 2), export. *Connects to: RF07, RF06, RF05.*

**Screen 5 — Action Plans:** simple Kanban board (columns "A Fazer" / "Em Andamento" / "Concluído") with static example cards. *(Extension — section 2.)*

**Screen 6 — Settings and profile:** evolution dashboard, persona selector — "Analítico" / "Empático" / "Socrático" (extension, section 2; it would only change the system-prompt string of RF04), delete account. *Connects to: RF09, RNF05.*

---

## 6. Backend endpoint inventory

The backend is already built and frozen. The API contract, `docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml`, is the source of truth; this section is a reading of it oriented by screen and requirement. How to build the real URL of each operation: `docs/input/backend/README.md`.

Every endpoint returns errors in the standard contract of RNF09 — `{ code, message, retryable }` — and is protected by RLS in Supabase. AI providers: Claude (chat, vision/OCR, summary, insights, dashboard, PII detection) and Voyage AI (embeddings) — the backend's only two external AI dependencies. Audio transcription (speech-to-text) runs on-device (Whisper) and never reaches the backend as an audio file.

### 6.1 Authentication and session
| Endpoint | Requirement | AI involved |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /auth/signup` | RF03 | — |
| `POST /auth/login` | RF03 | — |
| `POST /auth/refresh` | RF03, RF07 | — |
| `GET /auth/session` | RF07 | — |
| `POST /auth/logout` | RF03 | — |

**No "biometric-unlock" endpoint — intentional:** the Face ID / Touch ID / PIN barrier of Screen 0.1 is validated entirely on the device, never on the server. The backend only stores the preference (`biometricEnabled`, read and written via `PATCH /account/settings`, section 6.7) — it validates no biometrics. After passing the local barrier, the app uses the existing session (renewed via `POST /auth/refresh` when needed, or `POST /auth/login` if it has fully expired).

### 6.2 Ingestion and entries
| Endpoint | Requirement | AI involved |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /media/ocr` — the image is not persisted; only the extracted text moves on | RF02 | Claude Haiku 4.5 (vision) |
| `POST /entries` — creates an entry; internally triggers the PII check and embedding generation; accepts `source` (`manual`/`audio`/`photo`/`chat`) and `chatMessageId` when the origin is the chat | RF01, RF02, RF10 | Claude Haiku 4.5 (PII) + Voyage AI (embedding) |
| `GET /entries` — filters by `source`/`dateFrom`/`dateTo`; tags appear only embedded in the response, read-only | RF07 | — |
| `GET /entries/:id` | RF07 | — |

**No entry editing or deletion, and no tag endpoint — intentional:** entries are immutable once created ("original content intact, never censored"); there is no `PATCH`/`DELETE /entries/:id`. Tags are populated only by test seed data — no endpoint creates, deletes or filters by tag or category (see RF06). This is consistent with section 2: dynamic categorization was simplified to manual tags that receive no functional implementation.

### 6.3 Chat and memory (RAG)

| `entries` | id, user_id, content, source (`manual`/`audio`/`photo`/`chat`), chat_message_id (nullable), embedding (vector, see 9), sync_status, created_at, updated_at | `embedding` generated in `POST /entries` via Voyage AI |
| `tags` | id, user_id, name | Extension — created manually by the user |
| `entry_tags` | entry_id, tag_id | N:N join table |
| `chat_sessions` | id, user_id, title, created_at | — |
| `chat_messages` | id, session_id, role (`user`/`assistant`), content, created_at | User messages show the RF10 button |
| `export_jobs` | id, user_id, status (`pending`/`processing`/`done`/`error`), period_start, period_end, file_url, created_at | Asynchronous — see 6.5 |

**RLS pattern (every table with `user_id`):** policy `auth.uid() = user_id`, no exceptions.

---

## 9. Technology stack

| Layer | Choice |
|---|---|
| Mobile app | Flutter, BLoC, Clean Architecture |
| Backend | Already built and frozen; consumed through its API |
| Infrastructure | Supabase (Postgres + pgvector + Storage + Auth + RLS) |
| Chat / vision / OCR / summary / insights / dashboard / PII | Claude Sonnet 5 (chat) + Claude Haiku 4.5 (the rest) — in the backend |
| Embeddings (RAG) | Voyage AI `voyage-4` — in the backend |
| Speech-to-text (audio transcription) | Whisper on-device (`whisper_ggml`); audio never reaches the backend |
| Error handling | `fpdart` (`Either<Failure, T>`) |
| Layer rule | RNF06 |
| Test coverage | RNF07 |

---

## 10. Configuration parameters

Fixed values — not to be reinterpreted.

| Parameter | Value | Requirement |
|---|---|---|
| Background session timeout | 5 min | RF03 |
| Search debounce | 300 ms | RF06 |
| Proactive insight trigger | 5 messages OR 2 min of inactivity | RF08 |
| Dashboard rendering scenarios | 0 / 1 / > 30 entries | RF09 |
| Minimum test coverage (domain) | ≥ 80% | RNF07 |
| Local UI latency | < 100 ms | RNF01 |
| Loading-indicator threshold | > 300 ms | RNF01 |
| Network-error scenarios tested | 5 endpoints × 3 failures = 15 | RNF09 |

---

## 11. Error codes (RNF09)

Every endpoint returns `{ code, message, retryable }`. Minimum codes the app handles:

| Code | Situation | `retryable` |
|---|---|---|
| `AUTH_EXPIRED` | Session expired, re-authentication needed | no |
| `AUTH_INVALID` | Invalid credentials / biometrics | no |
| `NETWORK_TIMEOUT` | Request exceeded the time limit | yes |
| `NETWORK_OFFLINE` | No connection — action blocked (see RF04/RF06) | yes |
| `VALIDATION_ERROR` | Malformed request body | no |
| `PII_CHECK_FAILED` | PII check failed before persisting | yes |
| `EMBEDDING_FAILED` | Voyage AI unavailable / error | yes |
| `AI_GENERATION_TIMEOUT` | Claude did not respond in time (chat/insight/summary/dashboard) | yes |
| `NOT_FOUND` | Resource does not exist or does not belong to the user | no |
| `RATE_LIMITED` | Request limit exceeded | yes |

The complete, closed list of the backend's 13 codes, with HTTP statuses, is in `docs/input/backend/error-taxonomy.md`.

---

## 12. Delivery order

Work is delivered in units, one per functional requirement, preceded by a foundation unit, in this order:

**F000 → RF03 → RF01 → RF02 → RF07 → RF06 → RF04 → RF10 → RF08 → RF05 → RF09**

- **F000 (foundation)** covers what no single requirement owns but all of them use: project scaffold, `design_tokens.dart`, HTTP client returning `Either`, login and sign-up (Screen 0.1a in the prototype), base navigation and expired-session handling.
- RF10 comes after RF01 and RF04; RF08 comes after RF04.

---

## 13. Technical constraints

**Fixed:**
- Flutter and Dart at the version pinned for the repository (fvm).
- State management: `flutter_bloc`.
- Clean Architecture, three layers per feature.
- Error handling: `fpdart`; repositories return `Either<Failure, T>`.
- Test doubles: `mocktail`.
- On-device speech-to-text: `whisper_ggml`.
- Visual tokens: `lib/core/design_tokens.dart` is the single source of colors, typography, spacing and radii.
- Platform: iOS, portrait only.
- Folder convention:

```
lib/
  core/
  features/
    <feature>/
      data/
      domain/
      presentation/
```

**Free (choose what fits):** routing, HTTP client, local cache, dependency injection, secure storage, biometrics package, chart package.

187	- **Asynchronous processing — audio transcription:** a loading state (spinner + frozen waveform) and two outcomes (success/error); the error always offers "Tentar novamente" and never loses the recorded audio.
188	- **Asynchronous processing — photo OCR:** same pattern as audio, with one extra exit on error: "Salvar só a foto", which saves the record even without extracted text.
189	- **Asynchronous processing — export:** two loading stages (preparing → generating the AI summary) before the result; on error, the raw data is always available for download — the failure is isolated to the AI narrative, never to the user's data.
190	- **Dashboard narrative unavailable:** the chart loads normally but the AI summary paragraph fails — distinct from "zero entries" (lack of data) and needs its own error message.
191	
192	---

195	
196	1. **"29 frames" vs. "32 states":** the prototype has 32 distinct navigable states, but the number of frames (29) suggests that some state families should be one screen with internal state, not separate routes (e.g., a single `ExportSheet` with a status enum instead of 5 routes). Consider this when designing navigation.
197	2. **Account deletion without a success screen:** both "Sair" and "Apagar tudo" return to the Biometria screen; there is no "account deleted" or "you signed out" screen.
198	3. **Login vs. sign-up:** the same screen toggled by a text link; the prototype shows no extra sign-up fields (e.g., password confirmation, name). Whether sign-up needs extra fields is a product decision not covered visually.
199	4. **Insertion modal when offline:** not represented.
200	5. **Switching tabs in the insertion modal:** opening the modal always resets every tab to `idle`/empty, but switching tabs *during* a modal session is not cleared automatically — the expected behavior (e.g., whether an ongoing recording is discarded on tab switch) is not defined by the prototype.
201	6. **Per-entry sync indicator:** the states "sincronizado / sincronizando / erro de sync" exist visually on the cards, but no explicit "retry sync" action is shown for the error state. The semantics of the badge are in `docs/input/backend/sync-badge.md`.
202	7. **Text search combined with filters:** the filter sheet and the text search are on the same screen, but the prototype does not show them acting together.
203	
204	---
205	
206	## 6. Component library
207	
208	| Component | Where it appears | Variations |
209	|---|---|---|
210	| Primary button | Auth, modals, sheets, confirmations | normal (`#1F3D34`) · pressed (`#16281F`, darker) · disabled (`#E1DACB` background, `#6B6255` text) |
211	| Secondary button (outline) | "Tentar novamente", "Cancelar", "Baixar dados brutos" | `#1F3D34` outline, no fill |
212	| Text button (ghost) | Mode-toggle links, "Fechar", "Limpar" | no background, `#1F3D34` or `#6B6255` depending on context |
213	| Text field | Login, Texto tab, name editing | empty · focused (1.5px `#1F3D34` border) · error (`#B3402A` border) |
214	| Chat bubble | Home/Chat | user (light green, straight bottom-right corner) · AI (ivory with shadow, straight bottom-left corner) · streaming (pulsing cursor at the end of the text) |
215	| Insight card | Home/Chat | ochre spine, mono label "INSIGHT", dismiss button |
216	| Bookmark button (RF10) | User messages in the chat | idle (outline) · saving (spinner) · saved (ochre check) · error (red warning) |
217	| Send-error banner | Home/Chat | "Não foi possível enviar — toque para tentar novamente"; background `rgba(179,64,42,.08)`, warning icon, red text |
218	| Offline banner | Home/Chat | blue-gray background `#5C7A93`, `ph-wifi-slash` icon, light text |
219	| Sync badge | Record cards (Tela 4) | synced (green dot) · synchronizing (ochre dot) · sync error (red dot) |
220	| Filter chip | Filter sheet, active filters | single choice (date) · multiple choice (category, type) · removable with "x" (active filters) |
221	| Record card | Tela 4 | spine colored by origin (manual = dark green, audio = olive green, photo = gray, chat = ochre) |
222	| Kanban card **[ext]** | Planos de Ação | spine by column (to do / in progress / done) |
223	| Initials avatar | Side menu, Configurações | dark green circle, 1–2 uppercase initials, two sizes (40px in the menu, 52px in Configurações) |
224	| AI persona card **[ext]** | Configurações | not selected (thin border) · selected (thick `#1F3D34` border + check icon) |
225	| Bar chart (dashboard) | Configurações | populated (10 bars) · one bar · empty (placeholder icon) |
226	| Export status card | Tela 4 (bottom sheet) | pending · processing · done · error · empty |
227	| Confirmation dialog | Sessão expirada, Confirmar exclusão | background scrim + centered card; neutral title (session) or red title (destructive deletion) |
228	| PIN keypad | Tela 0.1b/c | digits 0–9 + backspace; progress dots above |
229	| Tab bar | Insertion modal | 3 tabs (Texto/Áudio/Foto), active tab with filled background |

Splash (auto, 1.8 s)
  └─> Biometria ──tap/error──> PIN inicial / PIN após falha
  │      └─> "usar e-mail e senha" ──> Entrar / criar conta (toggle)
  │                                          └─> submit ──> Home/Chat
  └─(PIN complete, 4 digits)──> Home/Chat
  └─(Face ID/Touch ID ok)──> Home/Chat

Home/Chat (base screen)
  ├─ overlay: Sessão expirada (backend session expires; "Entrar novamente" ──> Biometria)
  ├─ overlay: side menu (☰ icon) ──> Meus Registros | Planos de Ação | Configurações | new conversation
  └─ overlay: Insertion modal ("+" button) ──> tabs Texto / Áudio / Foto, each with its own sub-states
        (on save, the modal closes and returns to Home/Chat with the record added)

Meus Registros (base screen, from the side menu)
  ├─ empty state (no records) ──CTA "Criar primeiro registro"──> Insertion modal
  ├─ overlay: filter sheet ──"Aplicar"──> active filters (chips on the list)

Planos de Ação (base screen, from the side menu) — static screen, 3-column kanban (extension, not implemented)

Configurações (base screen, from the side menu)
  ├─ dashboard variations: zero entries | one entry | more than 30 (with narrative) | narrative unavailable
  ├─ inline profile-name editing
  ├─ AI persona selection (Analítico / Empático / Socrático) (extension, not implemented)
  ├─ "Sair" ──> Biometria
  └─ overlay: account-deletion confirmation ──"Apagar tudo"──> Biometria (same destination as logout)
```

---

## 2. Navigable states

Names as they appear in the prototype. The prototype's own state catalog has 32 entries: Tela 0 — Splash; Tela 0.1 — Biometria; Tela 0.1a — Entrar / criar conta; Tela 0.1b — PIN inicial; Tela 0.1c — PIN após falha; Tela 1 — Home / Chat; Tela 2 — Texto, Áudio (Gravando, Processando, Transcrito, Erro), Foto (Captura, Processando OCR, Reconhecido, Erro); Tela 3 — Menu lateral; Tela 1 — Sessão expirada; Tela 4 — Meus Registros, Estado vazio, Sheet de filtro, Filtros ativos; Exportar — Pendente, Processando, Concluído, Erro, Período vazio; Tela 5 — Planos de Ação **[ext]**; Tela 6 — Configurações, Dashboard zero entradas, Dashboard uma entrada, Narrativa indisponível, Confirmar exclusão. The tables below group them by screen; some rows describe variations inside one state (e.g., the bookmark sub-states, the streaming response). Extension states (requirements, section 2) are marked **[ext]**.

### 2.1 Entry and authentication
| State | What it shows |

| Tela 0 — Splash | Wordmark "Cerne" centered on dark green, 3 loading dots; lasts 1.8 s and moves on automatically. |
| Tela 0.1 — Biometria | Fingerprint circle, title "Toque para desbloquear", link "Usar PIN", secondary link "usar e-mail e senha" near the bottom. |
| Tela 0.1a — Entrar | Login mode: title "Bem-vindo de volta", fields E-mail and Senha, CTA "Entrar", toggle link, link "usar biometria". |
| Tela 0.1a — Criar conta | Same screen in sign-up mode: title "Crie sua conta", CTA "Criar conta" (toggled by a text link, not a separate screen). |
| Tela 0.1b — PIN inicial | Title "Digite seu PIN", 4 progress dots, 3×4 numeric keypad with backspace; after the 4th digit, moves on after 350 ms. |
| Tela 0.1c — PIN após falha | Same as 0.1b plus the error band "Não foi possível reconhecer — digite seu PIN". |

### 2.2 Conversation
| State | What it shows |

| Tela 1 — Home/Chat (default) | Messages going back and forth; dark green fixed header with ☰ and wordmark; composer with "+", placeholder "Escreva uma mensagem...", send icon. |
| Tela 1 — Streaming | AI response revealed progressively with a pulsing cursor. |
| Tela 1 — Insight | Insight card with ochre spine, label "INSIGHT", "x" to dismiss, interleaved in the messages. |
| Tela 1 — Falha ao gerar resposta | Incomplete AI message with "Falha ao gerar resposta — toque para tentar novamente" in red, in place of the time. |
| Tela 1 — Bookmark | Bookmark on each user message with 4 sub-states: `idle`, `saving` (spinner), `saved` (ochre check), `error` (red warning). |
| Tela 1 — Offline | Blue-gray banner "Sem conexão — histórico disponível, novas mensagens bloqueadas"; send icon disabled. |
| Tela 1 — Sessão expirada | Light scrim over the chat (still readable), centered card with lock icon, title "Sessão expirada", text saying history and scroll position are kept, button "Entrar novamente". |

| Áudio — Processando | Spinner in place of stop; frozen, faded waveform (opacity .35); text "Transcrevendo..."; label "00:42 de áudio". |

| Áudio — Erro | Red warning icon, "Não foi possível transcrever", outline button "Tentar novamente". |
| Foto — Captura | Two large buttons, "Câmera" and "Galeria". |
| Foto — Processando OCR | Photo thumbnail, spinner, "Reconhecendo texto...". |
| Foto — Reconhecido | Small thumbnail next to the extracted (editable) text; "Salvar". |
| Foto — Erro | Thumbnail kept, warning icon, "Não foi possível reconhecer o texto", button "Tentar novamente" and secondary text action "Salvar só a foto". |

### 2.4 Records
| State | What it shows |
|---|---|
| Tela 4 — Meus Registros (default) | Records grouped by date ("Hoje", "Ontem", dates); each card with a spine colored by origin, source icon, time, sync indicator (green "sincronizado" / ochre "sincronizando" / red "erro de sync"), text excerpt, category chips when present; header with back arrow, title, download icon; search bar "Buscar nos registros..." with a funnel button. |
| Tela 4 — Vazio | Large notebook icon, "Nenhum registro ainda", CTA "Criar primeiro registro". |

### 2.5 Export (bottom sheet over Tela 4; 5 states)

| Processando | "Gerando resumo com IA...", progress bar. |

| Erro | Red warning; text explaining that the AI narrative failed but the data remains available; only the button "Baixar dados brutos". |
| Período vazio | "Nenhum registro nesse período." and a suggestion to adjust the filter; no download button. |

All five have the link "Fechar" at the bottom. The mapping between these states and the backend job statuses is in `docs/input/backend/export-screen-states.md`.

### Micro-animations and transitions
- `scrimIn` (0.18 s ease-out): fade of the darkened background when any overlay opens.
- `sheetUp` (0.2 s ease-out): bottom sheets (insertion modal, filter, export) rise from the bottom of the screen.
- Continuous spinner (`spin`, 1 s linear infinite) in every loading state.
- Text streaming: the AI response is revealed progressively, with a blinking cursor at the end while it is "typing".
- PIN: after the 4th digit, a 350 ms pause before navigating.

---

## 4. Special states that need extra care

- **Expired session:** an overlay on the chat that keeps history and scroll position — the expired token must not discard the conversation state in memory before re-authentication. Re-authenticating goes back to the Biometria screen, not to a full form.
- **Offline:** blocks **sending new messages** (send icon disabled, explanatory banner), but **history stays visible and navigable**. The prototype does not show what happens to the insertion modal (text/audio/photo) when offline.
- **Asynchronous processing — audio transcription:** a loading state (spinner + frozen waveform) and two outcomes (success/error); the error always offers "Tentar novamente" and never loses the recorded audio.
- **Asynchronous processing — photo OCR:** same pattern as audio, with one extra exit on error: "Salvar só a foto", which saves the record even without extracted text.
- **Asynchronous processing — export:** two loading stages (preparing → generating the AI summary) before the result; on error, the raw data is always available for download — the failure is isolated to the AI narrative, never to the user's data.
- **Dashboard narrative unavailable:** the chart loads normally but the AI summary paragraph fails — distinct from "zero entries" (lack of data) and needs its own error message.

---

## 5. Implementation notes

1. **"29 frames" vs. "32 states":** the prototype has 32 distinct navigable states, but the number of frames (29) suggests that some state families should be one screen with internal state, not separate routes (e.g., a single `ExportSheet` with a status enum instead of 5 routes). Consider this when designing navigation.
2. **Account deletion without a success screen:** both "Sair" and "Apagar tudo" return to the Biometria screen; there is no "account deleted" or "you signed out" screen.
3. **Login vs. sign-up:** the same screen toggled by a text link; the prototype shows no extra sign-up fields (e.g., password confirmation, name). Whether sign-up needs extra fields is a product decision not covered visually.
4. **Insertion modal when offline:** not represented.
5. **Switching tabs in the insertion modal:** opening the modal always resets every tab to `idle`/empty, but switching tabs *during* a modal session is not cleared automatically — the expected behavior (e.g., whether an ongoing recording is discarded on tab switch) is not defined by the prototype.
6. **Per-entry sync indicator:** the states "sincronizado / sincronizando / erro de sync" exist visually on the cards, but no explicit "retry sync" action is shown for the error state. The semantics of the badge are in `docs/input/backend/sync-badge.md`.
7. **Text search combined with filters:** the filter sheet and the text search are on the same screen, but the prototype does not show them acting together.

---

## 6. Component library

| Primary button | Auth, modals, sheets, confirmations | normal (`#1F3D34`) · pressed (`#16281F`, darker) · disabled (`#E1DACB` background, `#6B6255` text) |
| Secondary button (outline) | "Tentar novamente", "Cancelar", "Baixar dados brutos" | `#1F3D34` outline, no fill |
| Text button (ghost) | Mode-toggle links, "Fechar", "Limpar" | no background, `#1F3D34` or `#6B6255` depending on context |
| Text field | Login, Texto tab, name editing | empty · focused (1.5px `#1F3D34` border) · error (`#B3402A` border) |
| Chat bubble | Home/Chat | user (light green, straight bottom-right corner) · AI (ivory with shadow, straight bottom-left corner) · streaming (pulsing cursor at the end of the text) |
| Insight card | Home/Chat | ochre spine, mono label "INSIGHT", dismiss button |
| Bookmark button (RF10) | User messages in the chat | idle (outline) · saving (spinner) · saved (ochre check) · error (red warning) |
| Send-error banner | Home/Chat | "Não foi possível enviar — toque para tentar novamente"; background `rgba(179,64,42,.08)`, warning icon, red text |
| Offline banner | Home/Chat | blue-gray background `#5C7A93`, `ph-wifi-slash` icon, light text |
| Sync badge | Record cards (Tela 4) | synced (green dot) · synchronizing (ochre dot) · sync error (red dot) |
| Filter chip | Filter sheet, active filters | single choice (date) · multiple choice (category, type) · removable with "x" (active filters) |
| Record card | Tela 4 | spine colored by origin (manual = dark green, audio = olive green, photo = gray, chat = ochre) |
| Kanban card **[ext]** | Planos de Ação | spine by column (to do / in progress / done) |
| Initials avatar | Side menu, Configurações | dark green circle, 1–2 uppercase initials, two sizes (40px in the menu, 52px in Configurações) |
| AI persona card **[ext]** | Configurações | not selected (thin border) · selected (thick `#1F3D34` border + check icon) |
| Bar chart (dashboard) | Configurações | populated (10 bars) · one bar · empty (placeholder icon) |
| Export status card | Tela 4 (bottom sheet) | pending · processing · done · error · empty |
| Confirmation dialog | Sessão expirada, Confirmar exclusão | background scrim + centered card; neutral title (session) or red title (destructive deletion) |
| PIN keypad | Tela 0.1b/c | digits 0–9 + backspace; progress dots above |
| Tab bar | Insertion modal | 3 tabs (Texto/Áudio/Foto), active tab with filled background |

1	# Feature Specification: P-RF03 — Biometric authentication vault
2	
3	**Feature Branch**: `002-biometric-auth-vault` (spec directory only — no git branch was created automatically; none of this repo's extension hooks are configured)
4	
5	**Created**: 2026-10-11
6	
7	**Status**: Draft
8	
9	**Input**: User description: "P-RF03 — Biometric authentication vault: Protect access to the user's data with a Face ID / Touch ID / PIN barrier, validated on the device, per docs/input/requirements.md section 1 (RF03) and section 10 (parameters), matching the prototype states 'Tela 0.1 — Biometria', 'Tela 0.1b — PIN inicial', 'Tela 0.1c — PIN após falha'. No biometric endpoint exists on the backend; the biometrics preference is stored via PATCH /account/settings, and the session is renewed with POST /auth/refresh or POST /auth/login after passing the barrier. Depends on F000 (session, login). Do not implement features of later units, extension features, or change the backend."
10	
11	## Clarifications
12	
13	### Session 2026-10-11
14	
15	- Q: During first-time PIN setup, if the user opts into Face ID/Touch ID and the `PATCH /account/settings` call to save `biometricEnabled` fails (timeout, no connection, etc.), should that block the user from reaching Home/Chat, or should the app proceed locally and let the write resolve/retry in the background? → A: Proceed locally and retry in the background — the local PIN and the on-device biometric toggle already work regardless of backend reachability; first-time setup does not block on this write succeeding, consistent with the local-first philosophy of FR-002 and FR-015 (resolved by technical judgment per user direction, applying Constitution Principle I).
16	
17	## User Scenarios & Testing *(mandatory)*
18	
19	### User Story 1 - Unlocking the app with Face ID / Touch ID (Priority: P1)
20	
21	A returning user who has already set up the vault opens the app (cold launch) or brings it back from the background after a long pause. Before anything from their journal or chat becomes visible, they are asked to confirm their identity with Face ID or Touch ID. On success, the app proceeds exactly as it would have without the vault.
22	
23	**Why this priority**: This is the barrier itself — the entire reason the unit exists. Without it, no access protection exists at all.
24	
25	**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by launching the app on a device with biometrics enrolled and the vault already configured, confirming the biometric prompt appears before any data is visible, and confirming a successful scan proceeds into the app's normal session routing.
26	
27	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
28	
29	1. **Given** a device with a PIN already configured and Face ID/Touch ID enabled, **When** the app is cold-launched, **Then** the biometric prompt appears before any journal or chat content is shown, and a successful scan proceeds to the app's existing session routing (Home/Chat or login, depending on session validity).
30	2. **Given** the app was sent to the background and brought back after 5 minutes or more, **When** it resumes, **Then** the biometric prompt appears again before the previous screen becomes visible or interactive.
31	3. **Given** the app was sent to the background and brought back in under 5 minutes, **When** it resumes, **Then** no authentication is required and the user sees exactly the screen and state they left.
32	
33	---
34	
35	### User Story 2 - Biometric failure falls back to PIN (Priority: P1)
36	
37	A user's fingerprint or face is not recognized (bad lighting, wet finger, a scan error). Rather than being stuck, they are immediately offered their PIN as an alternative and can still get into the app.
38	
39	**Why this priority**: Explicit acceptance criterion in the requirement — a failed biometric read must never lock the user out, since biometric sensors fail routinely under normal conditions.
40	
41	**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by forcing a biometric failure (denied, cancelled, or not recognized) and confirming the PIN screen appears with an error message, then confirming a correct PIN still unlocks the app.
42	
43	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
44	
45	1. **Given** the biometric prompt is shown, **When** the scan fails or is not recognized, **Then** the PIN entry screen appears showing the error message "Não foi possível reconhecer — digite seu PIN", without any other interruption.
46	2. **Given** the PIN screen shown after a biometric failure, **When** the user enters the correct 4-digit PIN, **Then** the app unlocks and proceeds normally.
47	3. **Given** the PIN screen shown after a biometric failure, **When** the user enters an incorrect PIN, **Then** the error state remains, the entered digits are cleared, and the user can try again with no limit that locks them out of the app entirely.
48	
49	---
50	
51	### User Story 3 - Setting up the PIN for the first time (Priority: P2)
52	
53	Right after a user's very first successful login or sign-up on a device, before they can use the app, they are asked to choose a 4-digit PIN and confirm it. This PIN becomes the fallback that always works, whether or not biometrics are set up.
54	
55	**Why this priority**: Every later unlock (Story 1 and 2) depends on a PIN already existing; without this step the vault has nothing to fall back to.
56	
57	**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by signing up or logging in for the first time on a device with no PIN configured, confirming the create-PIN screen appears before Home/Chat, and confirming a matching confirmation proceeds while a mismatched one does not.
58	
59	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
60	
61	1. **Given** a user has just completed their first successful login or sign-up on a device with no PIN configured yet, **When** that happens, **Then** they are asked to enter a new 4-digit PIN and then re-enter it to confirm, before reaching Home/Chat.
62	2. **Given** the PIN confirmation step, **When** the re-entered PIN matches the first entry, **Then** the PIN is saved on the device and the user proceeds to Home/Chat.
63	3. **Given** the PIN confirmation step, **When** the re-entered PIN does not match, **Then** the user sees a clear message and is returned to entering a new PIN, without the mismatched PIN being saved.
64	4. **Given** the device supports Face ID or Touch ID, **When** PIN setup completes, **Then** the user is offered the option to also enable biometric unlock, and their choice is saved as their biometrics preference.
65	
66	---
67	
68	### User Story 4 - Recovering access via full login (Priority: P3)
69	
70	A user who cannot pass biometrics or does not remember their PIN taps a visible link on the vault screen and is taken to the regular email/password login, regaining access that way instead of being stuck.
71	
72	**Why this priority**: A safety valve for the barrier itself; it depends on the vault screen (Story 1) existing, and reuses login machinery that F000 already built, so it carries the least new risk of the four stories.
73	
74	**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by tapping "usar e-mail e senha" from the vault screen and confirming it leads to the existing login screen, where submitting valid credentials proceeds into the app.
75	
76	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
77	
78	1. **Given** the vault screen (biometric or PIN) is shown, **When** the user taps "usar e-mail e senha", **Then** they are taken to the existing login screen.
79	2. **Given** a user who reached login this way, **When** they submit valid credentials, **Then** they proceed into the app the same way a first-time login would.
80	
81	---
82	
83	### Edge Cases
84	
85	- A device has no biometric hardware, or no fingerprint/face enrolled at the OS level: the vault shows the PIN screen directly as the only method, without attempting or showing a fingerprint prompt first.
86	- The app process is killed by the operating system while backgrounded (not merely suspended): the next launch is treated as a cold launch and always shows the vault, regardless of how little time has passed.
87	- A user disables biometrics at the OS level (outside the app) between sessions: the next vault appearance falls back to PIN entry directly, with no error shown for the missing biometric capability.
88	- The background timer sits exactly at the 5-minute boundary: fewer than 5 minutes elapsed never re-prompts; 5 minutes or more always does.
89	- The app is killed mid-way through first-time PIN setup (Story 3) before confirmation completes: relaunching resumes the PIN setup flow rather than leaving the user in an unusable, PIN-less state.
90	- Repeated incorrect PIN entries: never produce a hard lockout of the app; the user can always retry or fall back to "usar e-mail e senha".
91	- The `PATCH /account/settings` call that saves the biometrics preference during first-time setup fails (timeout, no connection, malformed response): PIN setup still completes and the user still reaches Home/Chat; the write is not retried synchronously as part of the setup flow.
92	
93	## Requirements *(mandatory)*
94	
95	### Functional Requirements
96

# Feature Specification: P-RF03 — Biometric authentication vault

**Feature Branch**: `002-biometric-auth-vault` (spec directory only — no git branch was created automatically; none of this repo's extension hooks are configured)

**Created**: 2026-10-11

**Status**: Draft

**Input**: User description: "P-RF03 — Biometric authentication vault: Protect access to the user's data with a Face ID / Touch ID / PIN barrier, validated on the device, per docs/input/requirements.md section 1 (RF03) and section 10 (parameters), matching the prototype states 'Tela 0.1 — Biometria', 'Tela 0.1b — PIN inicial', 'Tela 0.1c — PIN após falha'. No biometric endpoint exists on the backend; the biometrics preference is stored via PATCH /account/settings, and the session is renewed with POST /auth/refresh or POST /auth/login after passing the barrier. Depends on F000 (session, login). Do not implement features of later units, extension features, or change the backend."

## Clarifications

### Session 2026-10-11

- Q: During first-time PIN setup, if the user opts into Face ID/Touch ID and the `PATCH /account/settings` call to save `biometricEnabled` fails (timeout, no connection, etc.), should that block the user from reaching Home/Chat, or should the app proceed locally and let the write resolve/retry in the background? → A: Proceed locally and retry in the background — the local PIN and the on-device biometric toggle already work regardless of backend reachability; first-time setup does not block on this write succeeding, consistent with the local-first philosophy of FR-002 and FR-015 (resolved by technical judgment per user direction, applying Constitution Principle I).

## User Scenarios & Testing *(mandatory)*

### User Story 1 - Unlocking the app with Face ID / Touch ID (Priority: P1)

A returning user who has already set up the vault opens the app (cold launch) or brings it back from the background after a long pause. Before anything from their journal or chat becomes visible, they are asked to confirm their identity with Face ID or Touch ID. On success, the app proceeds exactly as it would have without the vault.

**Why this priority**: This is the barrier itself — the entire reason the unit exists. Without it, no access protection exists at all.

**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by launching the app on a device with biometrics enrolled and the vault already configured, confirming the biometric prompt appears before any data is visible, and confirming a successful scan proceeds into the app's normal session routing.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** a device with a PIN already configured and Face ID/Touch ID enabled, **When** the app is cold-launched, **Then** the biometric prompt appears before any journal or chat content is shown, and a successful scan proceeds to the app's existing session routing (Home/Chat or login, depending on session validity).
2. **Given** the app was sent to the background and brought back after 5 minutes or more, **When** it resumes, **Then** the biometric prompt appears again before the previous screen becomes visible or interactive.
3. **Given** the app was sent to the background and brought back in under 5 minutes, **When** it resumes, **Then** no authentication is required and the user sees exactly the screen and state they left.

---

### User Story 2 - Biometric failure falls back to PIN (Priority: P1)

A user's fingerprint or face is not recognized (bad lighting, wet finger, a scan error). Rather than being stuck, they are immediately offered their PIN as an alternative and can still get into the app.

**Why this priority**: Explicit acceptance criterion in the requirement — a failed biometric read must never lock the user out, since biometric sensors fail routinely under normal conditions.

**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by forcing a biometric failure (denied, cancelled, or not recognized) and confirming the PIN screen appears with an error message, then confirming a correct PIN still unlocks the app.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** the biometric prompt is shown, **When** the scan fails or is not recognized, **Then** the PIN entry screen appears showing the error message "Não foi possível reconhecer — digite seu PIN", without any other interruption.
2. **Given** the PIN screen shown after a biometric failure, **When** the user enters the correct 4-digit PIN, **Then** the app unlocks and proceeds normally.
3. **Given** the PIN screen shown after a biometric failure, **When** the user enters an incorrect PIN, **Then** the error state remains, the entered digits are cleared, and the user can try again with no limit that locks them out of the app entirely.

---

### User Story 3 - Setting up the PIN for the first time (Priority: P2)

Right after a user's very first successful login or sign-up on a device, before they can use the app, they are asked to choose a 4-digit PIN and confirm it. This PIN becomes the fallback that always works, whether or not biometrics are set up.

**Why this priority**: Every later unlock (Story 1 and 2) depends on a PIN already existing; without this step the vault has nothing to fall back to.

**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by signing up or logging in for the first time on a device with no PIN configured, confirming the create-PIN screen appears before Home/Chat, and confirming a matching confirmation proceeds while a mismatched one does not.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** a user has just completed their first successful login or sign-up on a device with no PIN configured yet, **When** that happens, **Then** they are asked to enter a new 4-digit PIN and then re-enter it to confirm, before reaching Home/Chat.
2. **Given** the PIN confirmation step, **When** the re-entered PIN matches the first entry, **Then** the PIN is saved on the device and the user proceeds to Home/Chat.
3. **Given** the PIN confirmation step, **When** the re-entered PIN does not match, **Then** the user sees a clear message and is returned to entering a new PIN, without the mismatched PIN being saved.
4. **Given** the device supports Face ID or Touch ID, **When** PIN setup completes, **Then** the user is offered the option to also enable biometric unlock, and their choice is saved as their biometrics preference.

---

### User Story 4 - Recovering access via full login (Priority: P3)

A user who cannot pass biometrics or does not remember their PIN taps a visible link on the vault screen and is taken to the regular email/password login, regaining access that way instead of being stuck.

**Why this priority**: A safety valve for the barrier itself; it depends on the vault screen (Story 1) existing, and reuses login machinery that F000 already built, so it carries the least new risk of the four stories.

**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by tapping "usar e-mail e senha" from the vault screen and confirming it leads to the existing login screen, where submitting valid credentials proceeds into the app.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** the vault screen (biometric or PIN) is shown, **When** the user taps "usar e-mail e senha", **Then** they are taken to the existing login screen.
2. **Given** a user who reached login this way, **When** they submit valid credentials, **Then** they proceed into the app the same way a first-time login would.

---

### Edge Cases

- A device has no biometric hardware, or no fingerprint/face enrolled at the OS level: the vault shows the PIN screen directly as the only method, without attempting or showing a fingerprint prompt first.
- The app process is killed by the operating system while backgrounded (not merely suspended): the next launch is treated as a cold launch and always shows the vault, regardless of how little time has passed.
- A user disables biometrics at the OS level (outside the app) between sessions: the next vault appearance falls back to PIN entry directly, with no error shown for the missing biometric capability.
- The background timer sits exactly at the 5-minute boundary: fewer than 5 minutes elapsed never re-prompts; 5 minutes or more always does.
- The app is killed mid-way through first-time PIN setup (Story 3) before confirmation completes: relaunching resumes the PIN setup flow rather than leaving the user in an unusable, PIN-less state.
- Repeated incorrect PIN entries: never produce a hard lockout of the app; the user can always retry or fall back to "usar e-mail e senha".
- The `PATCH /account/settings` call that saves the biometrics preference during first-time setup fails (timeout, no connection, malformed response): PIN setup still completes and the user still reaches Home/Chat; the write is not retried synchronously as part of the setup flow.

- **FR-007**: When the app is sent to the background and brought back after 5 minutes or more have elapsed, the system MUST require the authentication barrier again before the previously visible screen becomes visible or interactive.
- **FR-008**: When the app is sent to the background and brought back in under 5 minutes, the system MUST NOT require re-authentication, and MUST resume exactly the screen and state the user left.

- **FR-013**: On a device where biometrics are available, the system MUST let the user optionally enable Face ID/Touch ID unlock as part of first-time PIN setup, and MUST persist that choice as the account's biometrics preference through the backend.
- **FR-014**: Persisting the biometrics preference MUST reuse the single typed-failure network call path already established by the foundation unit, not a separate or ad hoc HTTP call. If that call fails (timeout, no connection, malformed response), the failure MUST NOT block PIN setup from completing or the user from reaching Home/Chat — the local PIN and the on-device biometric toggle already govern unlocking regardless of backend reachability, and the preference write is left to resolve or retry through the existing failure-handling path.
- **FR-015**: Passing the local barrier MUST NOT by itself constitute backend authentication; the app MUST continue to rely on the session machinery already established (silent renewal, or a full login if the session can no longer be renewed).

### Key Entities

## Success Criteria *(mandatory)*

### Measurable Outcomes

- **SC-001**: 100% of cold launches and background resumes of 5 minutes or more show the authentication barrier before any user data becomes visible.
- **SC-002**: 100% of resumes from the background under 5 minutes skip authentication and restore the exact prior screen state.

A device with no PIN yet (first-ever app use before any account exists) is unaffected by this unit and continues straight to F000's existing login/sign-up flow; PIN setup is triggered immediately after that flow's first success (Story 3).

# Cerne Constitution

## Core Principles

### I. Product Source of Truth
`docs/input/` — `requirements.md`, `prototype/`, and `backend/` — is the
authoritative source for product behavior. `requirements.md` defines
functional and quality requirements, screens, the API surface, delivery
order, and technical constraints; `prototype/` is the frozen visual
reference and its token/state extract; `backend/` documents the existing
API, error taxonomy, screen-state map, sync-badge semantics, and fixtures.
Where these documents are silent, implementers MUST make a reasonable
technical decision rather than block on clarification. Files under
`docs/input/` are frozen inputs and MUST NOT be edited by anyone working in
this repository.

Rationale: a reflective-journaling app with a frozen, already-documented
backend has exactly one place where ambiguity should be resolved — the
product input — so decisions stay traceable and the backend contract stays
stable.

### II. Fixed Technology Stack
The app is built with Flutter and Dart at the version pinned via `fvm`,
using `flutter_bloc` for state management and Clean Architecture with three
layers per feature. Error handling MUST use `fpdart`, with every repository
returning `Either<Failure, T>`. Test doubles MUST use `mocktail`. Speech-to-
text runs on-device via `whisper_ggml`; audio content MUST NEVER be sent to
the backend. The shipping platform is iOS. Choices not fixed here — routing,
HTTP client, local cache, dependency injection, secure storage, biometrics,
and charting — are open implementation decisions.

Rationale: a single, non-negotiable stack removes a whole category of
architectural debate and keeps the codebase consistent across features
built by different contributors or at different times.

### III. Backend Boundary — Frozen Backend, No Direct AI Calls
The backend is already built and frozen. The app consumes it strictly as
documented in `docs/input/backend/`, including its API contract
(`docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml`); the app MUST NOT change the
backend, its API contract, or its configuration. All AI features, including
semantic search, are provided exclusively by the backend — the app MUST
NEVER call an AI provider directly. Configuration and credentials come from
a project-root `.env` with exactly two variables: `FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL` and
`SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`. Every call to `{FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL}/<function>` MUST
carry the header `apikey: <SUPABASE_ANON_KEY>`. The `Authorization: Bearer`
header carries `SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` for operations that need no user session
(sign-up, login, refresh) and the user's access token for every operation
marked `bearerAuth` in the OpenAPI contract. `.env` and any credential MUST
NEVER be committed.

Rationale: the backend and its AI integrations are out of this project's
scope and already relied upon elsewhere; treating them as an immutable,
narrowly-accessed contract prevents scope creep and accidental coupling or
credential leakage.

### IV. Design Token Discipline & Visual Fidelity
`lib/core/design_tokens.dart` is the single source of colors, typography,
spacing, and radii. No visual value MAY be hardcoded anywhere else. The UI
MUST be faithful to `docs/input/prototype/`. UI text MUST be in Portuguese,
exactly as written in the prototype; code identifiers, comments, and project
documentation MUST be in English.

Rationale: a single token source makes visual fidelity (RNF08) mechanically
checkable, and separating UI language (Portuguese, matching the frozen
prototype) from code language (English) keeps the codebase reviewable while
preserving the product's voice.

### V. Clean Architecture Folder Convention
Code MUST follow the folder convention:
```
lib/
  core/
  features/
    <feature>/
      data/
      domain/
      presentation/

a project-root `.env` with exactly two variables: `FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL` and

carry the header `apikey: <SUPABASE_ANON_KEY>`. The `Authorization: Bearer`

marked `bearerAuth` in the OpenAPI contract. `.env` and any credential MUST
NEVER be committed.

scope and already relied upon elsewhere; treating them as an immutable,
narrowly-accessed contract prevents scope creep and accidental coupling or
credential leakage.

### IV. Design Token Discipline & Visual Fidelity
`lib/core/design_tokens.dart` is the single source of colors, typography,
spacing, and radii. No visual value MAY be hardcoded anywhere else. The UI
MUST be faithful to `docs/input/prototype/`. UI text MUST be in Portuguese,
exactly as written in the prototype; code identifiers, comments, and project
documentation MUST be in English.

Rationale: a single token source makes visual fidelity (RNF08) mechanically
checkable, and separating UI language (Portuguese, matching the frozen
prototype) from code language (English) keeps the codebase reviewable while
preserving the product's voice.

# Feature Specification: P-RF01 — Multimodal capture

**Feature Branch**: `003-multimodal-capture` (spec directory only — no git branch was created automatically; none of this repo's extension hooks are configured)

**Created**: 2026-10-12

**Status**: Draft

**Input**: User description: "P-RF01 — Multimodal capture: Let the user create a journal entry by text, audio recording or photo, from the Insertion Modal, per docs/input/requirements.md section 1 (RF01) and its acceptance criteria. Prototype states: Insertion modal — 'Texto', 'Áudio — Gravando', 'Foto — Captura' (prototype extract, section 2.3), opened by the '+' button of Home/Chat. Backend: POST /entries with source manual/audio/photo. Depends on F000, RF03. Do not implement features of later units, extension features (requirements section 2), or change the backend."

## Clarifications

### Session 2026-10-12

- Q: When a user stops recording audio or captures a photo in this unit, how should Save behave, given RF02 (speech-to-text/OCR) is an explicitly later unit and the prototype states listed for this unit stop at "Gravando" and "Captura"? → A: RF01 performs the minimal on-device transcription (audio) or backend OCR call (photo) needed to produce text content inline, as part of confirming Save, shown with only a plain/generic loading indicator — not RF02's dedicated "Processando / Transcrito / Reconhecido / Erro" screens, their editable-text review step, or their specific retry affordances ("Tentar novamente", "Salvar só a foto"). This is the only reading under which RF01 alone satisfies its own stated acceptance criterion that all three modalities "result in the same persisted-entry format," since entries are immutable (no `PATCH`/`DELETE /entries/:id`) and therefore cannot be corrected after creation — recognition must happen before the entry exists. (Resolved by technical judgment per user direction, applying Constitution Principle I, where the input docs are silent on this exact boundary.)

## User Scenarios & Testing *(mandatory)*

### User Story 1 - Writing a journal entry as text (Priority: P1)

A user wants to quickly note something in words. They tap "+" on Home/Chat, the Insertion Modal opens on its "Texto" tab, they write freely in the text field, and tap "Salvar". The modal closes and the note now exists as one of their journal entries.

**Why this priority**: The simplest and fully self-contained of the three capture paths — it has no dependency on recognition of any kind, so it is the first thing that must work end to end.

**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by tapping "+", typing text into the Texto tab, tapping "Salvar", and confirming a new entry with that exact text and origin "manual" now exists, and the modal has closed back to Home/Chat.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** Home/Chat is open, **When** the user taps "+", **Then** the Insertion Modal opens as an overlay on top of Home/Chat (which stays in place underneath), defaulted to the "Texto" tab with an empty field.
2. **Given** the Texto tab with text typed into the field, **When** the user taps "Salvar", **Then** a new journal entry is created with that text as its content and origin "manual", and the modal closes, returning to Home/Chat.
3. **Given** the Texto tab with an empty field, **When** the user looks at "Salvar", **Then** the action is unavailable (disabled), so an empty entry can never be created.

---

### User Story 2 - Recording a journal entry as audio (Priority: P1)

A user prefers to speak rather than type. They tap "+", switch to the "Áudio" tab, and recording begins with a visible waveform and timer. They tap stop, and after a brief moment the spoken content is saved as a journal entry just like a written one.

**Why this priority**: Voice capture is one of the two microphone/camera-dependent paths and, together with Story 1, establishes that every modality converges on the same entry format — the central acceptance criterion of this unit.

**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by opening the Áudio tab, recording a short spoken note, stopping the recording, confirming Save completes, and confirming a new entry exists with origin "audio" and text content derived from what was spoken.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** the Insertion Modal is open, **When** the user switches to the "Áudio" tab, **Then** recording starts immediately, showing a stop control, an animated waveform, and a running mm:ss timer.
2. **Given** an active recording, **When** the user taps stop, **Then** the recording ends and the system automatically transcribes it and completes the save as part of confirming the capture, producing one new entry with origin "audio" and the transcribed text as its content.
3. **Given** a completed audio capture that is being transcribed and saved, **When** that processing is underway, **Then** the user sees a plain loading indicator (not a detailed multi-state screen) until it finishes.
4. **Given** transcription or the save itself fails (e.g., inaudible recording, network timeout), **When** that happens, **Then** no entry is created, a clear failure message is shown, and the user can retry without having to re-record, as long as the captured audio is still held locally.

---

### User Story 3 - Capturing a journal entry from a photo (Priority: P2)

A user has something written down on paper, a receipt, or a whiteboard. They tap "+", switch to the "Foto" tab, choose "Câmera" or "Galeria", and the text in the image becomes a journal entry.

**Why this priority**: Mirrors Story 2's recognition pipeline for a second input type; ordered after audio because the text-recognition concern it shares with Story 2 is already established there.
